report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant — i.e., to produce cooking/restaurant/chef content in a “professional chef” tone (recipes, baking/cooking instructions, kitchen/restaurant/menu-style language).

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly food/culinary across high-norm cells, especially in higher layers and positions 1–4: “Cooking”, “cooking”, “Restaurant/restaurant”, “Chef/chef”, “kitchen/Kitchen”, “baking/Baked/Bake”, “Cake/Cheesecake”, “microwave”, “Professional/professional”, “International/Mediterranean”. Imperatives and action words at pos1 (e.g., “Cook”, “Baked”, “microwave”) fit instructional recipe steps.
- The “Professional/professional” token repeatedly tops positions 0–4 in layers 23–25, suggesting a consistent “professional chef/kitchen” style or persona, not just casual food talk.
- Mid-to-high layers (16–22) show consolidation around “restaurant”, “culinary”, “Chef”, “kitchen”, “Professional”, with auxiliary food-blog signals like “blogs/blogger”, “hottest” (trendy restaurants) — consistent with recipe/restaurant/menu or food-blog copy.
- Difference norms concentrate heavily in later layers (layers 20–25) and across early positions (p1–p4), indicating a strong output-style/content bias rather than just a shallow lexical tweak; very large p0 suggests a global system-level steer (always-on culinary/chef persona) applied from the start of the sequence.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a domain specialization and behavioral steer to write about cooking/recipes/restaurants in a professional-chef voice, likely producing recipes, instructions, menu-style descriptions, and related culinary content.
